state.case_summary:
A man in his 80s without a prior history of arrhythmia presented to the emergency department with cough and shortness of breath during the COVID-19 pandemic. He subsequently developed palpitations.

On arrival:- Temperature: Afebrile- Heart rate: 89 beats/min- Respiratory rate: 26 breaths/min - Blood pressure: 107/68 mm Hg- Jugular venous pressure: normal- Cardiac auscultation: Regular rate and rhythm without murmurs, rubs, or gallops- Pulmonary auscultation: Inspiratory crackles in bilateral bases of the lungs

- Laboratory tests:  SARS-CoV-2 PCR test: Positive- ECG findings:  - Regular, narrow complex tachycardia with rate of 170 beats/min  - T waves in inferior leads terminate with negative deflection corresponding to P wave in lead V1  - Superiorly directed P waves (negative in leads II, III, and aVF)  - Long RP interval (RP interval > PR interval)  - Short P-wave duration, most evident in lead V1  - Echocardiogram:  Finding: Mild diastolic dysfunction- Images mentioned:  Image Title: Figure 1. Initial Electrocardiogram During the Episode of Palpitations  Image Title: Figure 2. RP Interval Examples
